rationale: C12 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the later farewell letter. Both open by marking the addressee's impending departure, review distinguished service and contributions, and close with the notably parallel formula “You take with you” followed by best wishes. C23 and C17 share the broader retirement-letter structure, appreciation of service, personal reassurance or association, and concluding wishes, but lack C12's strongest distinctive verbal correspondence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: After a long, honorable career you are relinquishing your post
shared_material.parent_excerpt: You will be leaving shortly to return to California
shared_material.explanation: Both begin by identifying an imminent departure before turning to an appraisal of the recipient's service.

shared_material.child_excerpt: your distinguished wartime record and your great contribution
shared_material.parent_excerpt: your tireless efforts ... your contribution to good government and for helping maintain peace in the world
shared_material.explanation: Each middle section praises a record of public service and a contribution extending to international peace.

shared_material.child_excerpt: You take with you in retirement the heartfelt thanks and the very best wishes of your many friends and associates. With these I warmly include my own.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: You take with you my best wishes and those of Mrs. Eisenhower ... and our affection
shared_material.explanation: The shared “You take with you” closing construction, carrying best wishes into the recipient's next stage, is the clearest evidence of reusable drafting language.
